verdict: Software carried IBM again — revenue rose 5% to $17.1B and net income jumped 26%, so IBM raised its full-year free-cash-flow outlook.

segments.name: Software
segments.note: Software — Red Hat hybrid cloud (+11%), data (+19%) and transaction processing (+9%), partly offset by automation (-3%). The profit engine, at an 82.5% gross margin.

segments.name: Consulting
segments.note: Consulting — flat in dollars (up 2% at constant currency) as clients stayed cautious on discretionary projects.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.note: Mainframes and servers — distributed infrastructure jumped 31% while IBM Z fell 20% a year after its big launch cycle.

segments.name: Financing
segments.note: Financing client purchases of IBM hardware and software.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Miscellaneous other revenue. IBM's release rounds segment lines and warns they may not add to totals — this line is shown $1M below the rounded $66M so the chart matches the reported $17,103M total.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative spending — sales teams and the back office.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Research and development, up 14% as IBM invests in AI and hybrid cloud.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $491M, partly offset by $164M of intellectual-property and custom-development income and $109M of other income — a net $218M cost, shown as $219M with the $1M rounding difference IBM flags in its release.

takeaways.title: Software did the lifting
takeaways.text: Software revenue rose 8% to $7.8B — Red Hat up 11% and data up 19% — while consulting was flat, which is why total growth was 5% and not more.

takeaways.title: Cash flow is the story
takeaways.text: Free cash flow reached $7.8B in the first nine months, and IBM now expects it to grow by more than $1B this year — funding the $1.69 quarterly dividend and $11.4B of acquisitions so far in 2026.

takeaways.title: GAAP margins still lag the adjusted ones
takeaways.text: GAAP pre-tax margin was 14.6% vs 19.3% on IBM's operating (non-GAAP) view — the gap is acquisition-related amortization and retirement-plan costs that adjusted figures exclude.

oneTimers: Discontinued operations lost $10M ($0.01 per share), so total net income was $2,190M vs $2,199M from continuing operations.
IBM ended the quarter with $63.8B of debt, including $12.7B of financing debt, after spending $11.4B on acquisitions this year.
